verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）我的心哪，你要称颂耶和华！凡在我里面的，也要称颂他的圣名！
verses.en: By David.Praise the Lord, O my soul.With all that is within me, praise[NOTE:1] his holy name.
notes: Psalm 103. The psalmist praises God for his mercy and willingness to forgive his people.
verses.commentary:
103:1-2,20-22 "Bless the Lord" When
one compares the first and last verses of this Psalm and Ps. 104:1,35, it is obvious that they
form a pair (six Piel IMPERATIVES). This is very unusual.

▣ "Bless" This term (BDB 138, KB 159)
is one of two roots used of blessings.

- אשר (BDB 80) is used 45 times in the OT and corresponds
to the "bless" of Matt. 5:3-10 (i.e. the Beatitudes). It denotes a state of blessedness
(cf. Ps. 1:1; 2:12; 32:1,2; 33:12; 34:8; 40:4; etc.).

- ברך (BDB 138) is used here (cf. Ps. 103:1,2,20,21,21; 104:1,35)
and over 325 times in the OT. It was used of

- YHWH blessing initial creation ‒ Gen. 1:22, 28

- YHWH blessing the Patriarchs ‒ Gen. 12:1; 18:18; 22:17-18; 26:4; 28:14

- the cursing and blessing of covenant obedience ‒ Deuteronomy 27-28 (also note Leviticus 26)

- The basic root has two (possibly related) connotations.

(1) to kneel

(2) to bless

103:1 "O my soul" This is a literary form
where the author speaks to himself (cf. Ps. 42:5,11; 43:5; 104:1,35; 116:7). It
is a way of referring to one's own thinking process.

▣ "soul" Nephesh (BDB 659,
KB 711-713) is the Hebrew term for "life force." It is used for both mankind
(Gen. 2:7) and the animals (cf. Gen. 1:24; 2:19). Here, it is parallel with the
next phrase, "all that is within me," which emphasizes the author's attempt to
praise YHWH with his whole being. See note online at Ps. 3:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

▣ "His holy name" The rest of this
Psalm, particularly Ps. 103:8-14, describes the character of YHWH. This Psalm
helps us to get a true picture of the heart and mind of the eternal, creator,
redeemer God.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 我的心哪，你要称颂耶和华！不可忘记他的一切恩惠！
verses.en: Praise the Lord, O my soul.Do not forget all his kind deeds.[NOTE:1]
notes: The verb “praise” is understood by ellipsis in the second line (see the preceding line).
verses.commentary:
103:2 "And forget none of His benefits"
In the OT, for God to forget is very important because it speaks of His pardon.
But for people to forget speaks of their ingratitude or rebellion. A good
parallel passage for YHWH's tender mercy toward fallen man is seen in Deut.
4:9,23,31; 6:12; 8:11,14,19; 9:7; 25:19. Just to sit and reflect on who God is
and what He has done for us brings joy to the heart of a true believer.

verses.zh: 他赦免你的一切罪孽，医治你的一切疾病。
verses.en: He is the one who forgives all your sins,who heals all your diseases,[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “his benefits” (see 2 Chr 32:25, where the noun is also used of kind deeds performed by the Lord).
verses.commentary:
103:3 "Who pardons all your iniquities"
The term (BDB 699, KB 757) for "pardons" is used in Hebrew only for God's
forgiveness. Psalm 103:11-13 includes three images that describe God's
forgiveness in graphic terms.

▣ Notice the series of PARTICIPLES that describe why YHWH should be
blessed (i.e. He gives benefits).

- He pardons all your iniquities ‒ BDB 699, KB 757, Qal

- He heals all your diseases ‒ BDB 950, KB 1272, Qal

- He redeems your life from the pit ‒ BDB 145, KB 169, Qal

- He crowns you with lovingkindness and compassion ‒ BDB 742, KB 815, Piel

- He satisfies your years with good things ‒ BDB 959, KB 1302, Hiphil

This series of five PARTICIPLES covers life on earth.

▣ "Who heals all your diseases" The Hebrew NOUN, "diseases"
(BDB 316), and VERB (BDB 317 I) are used in Deut. 29:21 in the sense
of cursing because of Israel's disobedience to the covenant. Because of this usage, and several
OT passages that speak of healing of sin (i.e. sickness as imagery for sin, cf. Ps. 41:4; Isa. 1:5-6; 6:10; 53:5;
1 Pet. 2:24-25), it is doubtful that the emphasis of this verse is on physical healing, although it surely includes that
(cf. Exod. 15:26; Deut. 32:29; Ps. 147:3; Matt. 8:14-17). The Jews recognized that sin and disease were related
(cf. John 9:2; James 5:13-18). Here, it is parallel to "pardons all your iniquities."

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEALING

verses.zh: 他救赎你的命脱离死亡，以仁爱和慈悲为你的冠冕。
verses.en: who delivers[NOTE:1] your life from the Pit,[NOTE:2] who crowns you with his loyal love and compassion,
notes: This relatively rare noun refers to deadly diseases (see Deut 29:22; Jer 14:18; 16:4; 2 Chr 21:19).
Or “redeems.”
verses.commentary:
103:4 "Who redeems your life" The term "redeems" (BDB 145, KB 169, Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) is the same as "the kinsman redeemer" or go'el
(BDB 145, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, cf. Job 19:25 and also the same
root in Ruth 4). Here, YHWH is described in intimate family terms, as He is in Ps. 103:13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

▣ "from the pit" This could be used in
the sense of physical destruction, but because of its parallel in relationship
to the term Sheol in Ps. 16:10, it seems to relate to the author's hope
in the afterlife (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?).
Some authors even connect Ps. 103:4b and 5 to this context.

▣ "Who crowns you with lovingkindness"
The verbal root (BDB 742, KB 815, Piel PARTICIPLE) can mean

- crown ‒ LXX and most English translations, עטרה

- surround ‒ JPSOA, NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 384, עטר

Both make sense in this context.

▣ "compassion" The term (BDB 933) is
often used of YHWH (cf. Exod. 33:19; Deut. 13:17; 30:3; 2 Kgs. 13:23; Isa. 14:1;
30:18; 49:10,13; 54:8,10; 55:7; 60:10). It was used in Ps. 102:14 to describe
the exiles' feelings about the destroyed temple (cf. Lam. 3:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT), #1

verses.zh: 他用美物使你所愿的得以知足，以致你如鹰返老还童。
verses.en: who satisfies your life with good things,[NOTE:1] so your youth is renewed like an eagle’s.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term שַׁחַת (shakhat, “pit”) is often used as a title for Sheol (see Pss 16:10; 30:9; 49:9; 55:24 HT [55:23 ET]).

Heb “who satisfies with the good of your ornaments.” The text as it stands makes little, if any, sense. The translation assumes an emendation of עֶדְיֵךְ (ʿedyekh, “your ornaments”) to עֹדֵכִי (ʿodekhi, “your duration; your continuance”), that is, “your life” (see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 18).
verses.commentary:
103:5 "Who satisfies your years with good things"
This is a very difficult verse to translate because of the uncertainty of the
Hebrew term, "years."

- Literally, it means "ornaments" (BDB 725, KB 791).

- The King James translation, "mouth," is obviously incorrect.

- The ASV translation, along with the Septuagint, and the Vulgate, have "desire," which
seems to be a derived meaning from the original term

- Most modern translations use a textual emendation to bring forth the concept of life
or prime of life (cf. NEB, RSV, REB and JPSOA).

- The AB (Michael Dahood, p. 26) sees it as referring to eternity (i.e. life with God in heaven).

- The UBS Text Project, p. 377, gives "ornaments" a "B" rating (some doubt) but suggests "your vitality."

- "your ornaments/jewellery ‒ עדיך, BDB 725, KB 791

- as long as you are ‒ עדכי, BDB 723, KB 786

▣ "so that your youth is renewed like the eagle" The concept of "eagle"
has caused some commentators to take this verse in two different ways.

- actually refers to the vigorous strength of eagles (cf. Isa. 40:31)

- the mythical allusion to the phoenix, a bird which comes back to life after death
(cf. RSV translation; possibly Job 29:18)

- eagles molting so as to get new feathers (NET Bible)

The term translated "eagle" (BDB 676) can refer to an eagle or
a vulture (see UBS, Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 82-84). In this context of YHWH's mercy and grace, "eagle" is the better
choice (note Exod. 19:4; Deut. 32:11; Isa. 40:31).

The VERB "renewed" (BDB 293, KB 293) is rare
(cf. 1 Sam. 11:14; 2 Chr. 15:8; 24:4,12; Job 10:17; Isa. 61:4; Lam. 5:21). It is used
only three times in the Psalter.

- Ps. 51:10 ‒ renew a steadfast spirit within me (Piel IMPERFECT)

- Ps. 103:5 ‒ renewed like an eagle (Hithpael IMPERFECT)

- Ps. 104:30 ‒ You renew the face of the ground (Piel IMPERFECT)

verses.zh: 耶和华施行公义，为一切受屈的人伸冤。
verses.en: The Lord does what is fair,and executes justice for all the oppressed.[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression your youth is renewed like an eagle’s may allude to the phenomenon of molting, whereby the eagle grows new feathers.
verses.commentary:
103:6,7 "The Lord performs righteous deeds" The
term "righteous deeds" is used two ways in the OT.

- to describe YHWH's holiness

- to describe YHWH's acts of salvation (i.e. deliverance)

It seems that in these two verses we have a description of the events of the
Exodus and of the Wilderness Wanderings. Therefore, this is a threefold thanksgiving for YHWH's act of grace in

- deliverance from Egypt

- in revealing Himself to Moses

- patience with the people during the wandering in the wilderness

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "And judgments for all who are oppressed"
There are two ways to interpret texts such as this one.

- YHWH cares for the weak, poor, and powerless (i.e. Exod. 22:22-24; Deut. 10:17-19; Ps. 68:5).

- Since the OT saw prosperity as a sign of God's favor, often the logical conclusion was
He had rejected the others because of their sins (i.e. Job, Psalm 73), but it is possible to
see God's repeatedly stated love for them as a literary way of showing/affirming His love
and care for all!

verses.zh: 他使摩西知道他的法则，叫以色列人晓得他的作为。
verses.en: The Lord revealed his faithful acts[NOTE:1] to Moses,his deeds to the Israelites.
notes: Heb “the Lord does fairness, and [acts of] justice for all the oppressed.”
verses.commentary:
103:7 "He made known His ways to Moses" "Ways" would refer to YHWH's revelation
(cf. Deut. 32:2-4; Ps. 18:30; 138:2,5) or YHWH's redemptive acts (cf. Ps. 67:2; 77:13-14; 145:17).
He revealed Himself to Moses, cf. Exodus 19-20; 33:13; Ps. 99:7. The OT is inspired,
eternal revelation (cf. Matt. 5:17-19), but it must be remembered that Jesus is the ultimate
revelation (cf. Matt. 5:21-48). He is the only proper interpreter of Scripture. He is Lord of Scripture!
Mosaic revelation still functions in sanctification but not in justification.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PAUL'S VIEWS OF THE MOSAIC LAW

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: ILLUMINATION

▣ "His ways" This is one of several terms used to describe YHWH's revelation. His way needs to become our way!

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

verses.zh: 耶和华有怜悯，有恩典，不轻易发怒，且有丰盛的慈爱。
verses.en: The Lord is compassionate and merciful;he is patient[NOTE:1] and demonstrates great loyal love.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “made known his ways.” God’s “ways” in this context are his protective and salvific acts in fulfillment of his promise (see also Deut 32:4; Pss 18:30; 67:2; 77:13 [note vv. 11-12, 14]; 138:5; 145:17).
Heb “slow to anger” (see Ps 86:15).
verses.commentary:
103:8 "The Lord is compassionate and gracious,
slow to anger and abounding in lovingkindness" This is the first phrase in a series
to describe the nature of YHWH. It is an allusion to Exod. 34:6,7. These attributes
of God are affirmed again and again in Scripture (cf. Num. 14:18; Deut. 4:31; Neh. 9:17;
Ps. 86:15; 145:8; Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2). Our only hope is in the character and changelessness of YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 他不长久责备，也不永远怀怒。
verses.en: He does not always accuseand does not stay angry.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and great of loyal love” (see Ps 86:15).
verses.commentary:
103:9 When one reads v. 9 in English it seems to imply that YHWH will not always have
patience with fallen humanity, but it is a Hebrew idiom for exactly the opposite (cf. Jer. 3:12)! He will always have patience
with His special creation (cf. Gen. 6:3; Isa. 57:16). Verse 9 cannot be the exact opposite of v. 10.

▣ The term "strive" (BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal IMPERFECT) is
a term that refers to legal charges (cf. Jer. 3:5,12). YHWH's heart is always willing to turn back
to us when we turn back to Him (cf. James 4:8)!

verses.zh: 他没有按我们的罪过待我们，也没有照我们的罪孽报应我们。
verses.en: He does not deal with us as our sins deserve;[NOTE:1] he does not repay us as our misdeeds deserve.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew verb נָטַר (natar) is usually taken to mean “to keep; to guard,” with “anger” being understood by ellipsis. The idiom “to guard anger” is then understood to mean “to remain angry” (see Lev 19:18; Jer 3:5, 12; Nah 1:2). However, it is possible that this is a homonymic root meaning “to be angry” (see HALOT 695 s.v. נטר).
Heb “not according to our sins does he do to us.”
verses.commentary:
103:10 "He has not dealt with us according to our sins nor rewarded us according to
our iniquities" Faithful followers are not punished in relation to their sin nor rewarded on
the basis of their efforts. This verse obviously continues the thought of Ps. 103:9, and Israel knew the truth of it well.

verses.zh: 天离地何等的高，他的慈爱向敬畏他的人也是何等的大！
verses.en: For as the skies are high above the earth,so his loyal love towers[NOTE:1] over his faithful followers.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and not according to our misdeeds does he repay us.”
For this sense of the verb גָבַר (gavar), see L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 17, 19.
verses.commentary:
103:11 "For as high as the heavens are above the earth" This is the first of three images
to describe the boundless grace of God.

For "heavens" see SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN and
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN. This same phrasing refers to God's work in Isa. 55:9.

▣ "those who fear Him" The VERB (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) denotes "respect," "awe." This phrase is a recurrent
characteristic of faithful followers (cf. Ps. 15:4; 25:12,14; 103:13; 118:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

verses.zh: 东离西有多远，他叫我们的过犯离我们也有多远！
verses.en: As far as the eastern horizon[NOTE:1] is from the west,[NOTE:2] so he removes the guilt of our rebellious actions[NOTE:3] from us.
notes: Heb “those who fear him.”
Heb “sunrise.”
Or “sunset.”
verses.commentary:
103:12 "As far as the east is from the west"
The Hebrew etymological roots of "east" and "west" refer to the rising and
setting sun. As the height of the heavens cannot compare with God's grace, so,
the expanse of the earth from horizon to horizon cannot compare with God's
grace. When one compares this with Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; and Micah 7:19, the full
theological impact of the grace of God is overwhelming! When God forgives, God forgets!

▣ "So far has He removed our transgressions
from us" The term "remove" (BDB 934, KB 1221) signifies "no relationship
with," which illustrates the complete removal of the penalty and guilt of sin by
a gracious God.

This is OT justification by grace! When God forgives (because
of who He is), He forgets (cf. Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:19)! Our
past is forgiven and forgotten! Now we must live godly lives into the future out of
overwhelming gratitude for the forgiveness and forgetfulness of YHWH.
Many believers can intellectually affirm the forgiveness of God, but they have
never embraced the forgetfulness of God!

Notice that in Ps. 103:12-13 there are two words that begin
with ר (r), and these appear twice. This is an obvious sound play (as is the
threefold ג (g) sound in Ps. 103:10 and 11).

verses.zh: 父亲怎样怜恤他的儿女，耶和华也怎样怜恤敬畏他的人！
verses.en: As a father has compassion on his children,[NOTE:1] so the Lord has compassion on his faithful followers.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew term פֶּשַׁע (peshaʿ, rebellious act”) is here used metonymically for the guilt such actions produce.
Or “sons,” but the Hebrew term sometimes refers to children in general.
verses.commentary:
103:13 "Just as a father has compassion on
his children" Here again is another family image to describe YHWH's
love (cf. Exod. 4:22; Deut. 1:31; 8:5; Ps. 27:10; Prov. 3:12; Isa. 49:15; 63:16;
64:8; Jer. 31:9; Hosea 11:1; Mal. 1:6). This is the possible origin of Jesus'
term to describe God as Father.

This verse was used in Judaism on the Day of Atonement (cf.
Leviticus 16). It was quoted when one of the two scapegoats was pushed over the
cliff (i.e. bore sin away from the camp).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL, I. E. #2

▣ "So the Lord has compassion on those who fear Him" It must be
remembered that, although YHWH's initiating grace is key in biblical faith (i.e. Eph. 2:8-9,10), He demands a response
be made by humankind in an initial and ongoing way (cf. Ps. 103:17,18 for a threefold emphasis on this conditional
aspect of mankind's part.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣ "fear" The VERBAL "fear" (BDB 431, KB 432, Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) denotes those who revere God by faith and faithfulness. See full note
on the positive and negative aspects of "fear" at Ps. 15:2-5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

verses.zh: 因为他知道我们的本体，思念我们不过是尘土。
verses.en: For he knows what we are made of;[NOTE:1] he realizes[NOTE:2] we are made of clay.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “those who fear him.”
Heb “our form.”
Heb “remembers.”
verses.commentary:
103:14 "He Himself knows our frame"
This is the Hebrew term yetzer (BDB 428), which means "intent." God knows our thoughts and yet
still loves us (cf. Gen. 6:5; 8:21). It is interesting that generally the rabbis did not believe in original sin (Genesis 3),
but held to the theory of the two yetzers (i.e. good intent and evil intent). They said that every person has
a black dog and white dog inside them and the one fed the most becomes the bigger and stronger. This is an
emphasis on human responsibility, which is certainly a half truth (
SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION/PREDESTINATION AND THE NEED FOR A THEOLOGICAL BALANCE;
and SPECIAL TOPIC: AGE OF ACCOUNTABILITY)

The NRSV and JPSOA see the VERB in Ps. 103:14a as referring to the creation
of Adam (Gen. 2:7; 3:19) or to all humans (Ps. 139:15). The TEV and NJB assume it refers to what humans are made of
(i.e. clay, dust, cf. Gen. 2:7).

▣ "He is mindful that we are but dust"
This imagery implies initial creation (cf. Gen. 2:7; 3:19; Job 34:15 Ps.
104:29; Eccl. 3:20; 12:7). It speaks of humanity's frailty (cf. Job 10:9; Ps.
78:39), which introduces the next section, Ps. 103:15-18.

verses.zh: 至于世人，他的年日如草一样。他发旺如野地的花，
verses.en: A person’s life is like grass.[NOTE:1] Like a flower in the field it flourishes,
notes: Heb “we [are] clay.”
verses.commentary:
103:15,16 "As for man, his days are like grass" This strophe (Ps. 103:15-18) is an emphasis on the eternality of
God and the insignificant finitude of mankind. This same imagery is used several times in the OT (cf. Job 14:1,2; Ps. 90:5,6; Isa. 40:6-8),
and in the NT (cf. 1 Pet. 1:24-25).

verses.zh: 经风一吹，便归无有；它的原处也不再认识它。
verses.en: but when the hot wind[NOTE:1] blows, it disappears,and one can no longer even spot the place where it once grew.
notes: Heb “[as for] mankind, like grass [are] his days.” The Hebrew noun אֱנוֹשׁ (ʾenosh) is used here generically of human beings. What is said is true of all mankind.

verses.zh: 但耶和华的慈爱归于敬畏他的人，从亘古到永远；他的公义也归于子子孙孙―
verses.en: But the Lord continually shows loyal love to his faithful followers[NOTE:1] and is faithful to their descendants,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[the] wind.” The word “hot” is supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “but the loyal love of the Lord [is] from everlasting to everlasting over those who fear him.”
verses.commentary:
103:17-18 These verses contain a threefold series which describes
mankind's need to respond to YHWH's initiating love (i.e. human freewill).

- Ps. 103:17, those who fear Him

- Ps. 103:18, those who keep His covenant

- Ps. 103:18, those who remember His precepts to do them

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

103:17 "the lovingkindness of the Lord" This
refers to His covenant faithfulness.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

▣ "from everlasting to everlasting"
This is the doubling of 'olam (BDB 761, cf. Ps. 90:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

▣ "And His righteousness to children's children" We learn from parts of the Pentateuch that YHWH
visits the iniquity of the father on the children to the third and fourth generation (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9). However, for those
who love Him He visits His blessings to the thousandth generation (cf. Deut. 5:10; 7:9)! Faith and faithfulness in
YHWH moves through families (cf. Deut. 4:9; 6:7,20-25; 11:19; 32:46), as do sin and rebellion.

verses.zh: 就是那些遵守他的约、记念他的训词而遵行的人。
verses.en: to those who keep his covenant,who are careful to obey his commands.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and his righteousness to sons of sons.”
verses.commentary:
103:18 "to do them" Obedience is crucial to the covenant. The sovereign God
initiates it and sets limits but demands that His people obey, cf. Deut. 4:2,6,9,40; 5:10,12,29,32; 6:2,3,17,25; 7:8,9,11,12). This
concept of hearing God's word and then obeying it is the Hebrew word Shema (BDB 1033, cf. Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3;
27:10; 33:7). Jesus made this same point in Luke 6:46!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

▣ "covenant" See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 耶和华在天上立定宝座；他的权柄（原文是国）统管万有。
verses.en: The Lord has established his throne in heaven;his kingdom extends over everything.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to those who remember his precepts to do them.”
verses.commentary:
103:19 "His sovereignty rules over all" The term "all" is a reference to the praise due God by the cosmos.
He made it; it praises Him, both animate and inanimate.

verses.zh: 听从他命令、成全他旨意、有大能的天使，都要称颂耶和华！
verses.en: Praise the Lord, you angels of his,you powerful warriors who carry out his decreesand obey his orders.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his kingdom rules over all.”
verses.commentary:
103:20 "Bless the Lord, you His angels" This describes the personal, conscious
servants of God (cf. Heb. 1:4-14). There has been some discussion about the term, "His hosts" (BDB 838) in Ps. 103:21, which some see as other
groups of angels. The term does usually mean "army." However, because of the inanimate praise of Ps. 103:22, others have seen "His host"
as referring to the starry heavens (cf. Deut. 4:19; Ps. 19:1-6).

Notice that as faithful followers must obey YHWH, so too, the angels must obey (cf. Heb. 1:6-14).

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord of Hosts

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELS

verses.zh: 你们作他的诸军，作他的仆役，行他所喜悦的，都要称颂耶和华！
verses.en: Praise the Lord, all you warriors of his,[NOTE:1] you servants of his who carry out his desires.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[you] mighty ones of strength, doers of his word, by listening to the voice of his word.”
Heb “all his hosts.”

verses.en: Praise the Lord, all that he has made,[NOTE:1] in all the regions[NOTE:2] of his kingdom.Praise the Lord, O my soul.

Heb “all his works,” which includes mankind.
verses.commentary:
103:22 All nature, animals, humans, and angels praise God (cf. Phil. 2:9-11). Blessing and praise are due the
Creator (Psalm 104) and Redeemer (Psalm 103) of all! I can hardly wait to be a part of this great choir (cf. Rev. 5:9-14)!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You
must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are
meant to be thought provoking, not definitive.

- What is the central truth of this Psalm?

- How is this Psalm related to Psalm 104?

- Is healing a specific promise in the atonement of Christ? (cf. Isa. 53:5)

- Is the covenant conditional or unconditional? Explain.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is one of the highwater marks of praise in the Psalter. It is a companion to Psalm 104.
Psalm 103 focuses on God as merciful Redeemer (YHWH, Ps. 103:1,6,8,13,17,19,20,21,22
[twice]), while Psalm 104 focuses on God's creative power (Elohim, Ps. 104:1,33).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

- This Psalm seems to move from

- personal experience

- to corporate worship

- to cosmic worship

- Brief Outline

- Praise to YHWH for His love to individuals, Ps. 103:1-5

- Praise to YHWH for His love to Israel, Ps. 103:6-14

- Praise to YHWH for His infinite love to finite man, Ps. 103:15-18

- Let everything praise the Lord, Ps. 103:19-22

1Bless the Lord, O my soul,

Who heals all your diseases;
